ready1_open_rewrite.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question 1
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The figure shows the motion graphs of objects A and B making straight-line motion starting from the same point. If the vertical axis y in the figure represents velocity, then during the time from 0 to t1, what is the relationship between the displacement magnitudes of A and B?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: A's displacement is less than B's displacement

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The figure shows the motion graphs of objects A and B making straight-line motion starting from the same point. If the vertical axis y in the figure represents velocity, then during the time from 0 to t1, what is the relationship between the displacement magnitudes of A and B?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: A's displacement is less than B's displacement
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis is t, and the vertical axis is y; the graph labeled A is a steeper slanted line, extending upward from a point on the t-axis to the right of O, and the graph labeled B extends upward to the right from near O. In the time interval from 0 to t1, B's graph is above A's graph and intersects A's graph at t1. Therefore, within 0 to t1, the area enclosed by B's graph and the t-axis is greater than the area enclosed by A's graph and the t-axis. Then reason: The question stem states that the vertical axis y represents velocity, so this is a velocity-time graph; the area under a velocity-time graph and enclosed with the time axis represents displacement magnitude. Since the area corresponding to B is larger within 0 to t1, B's displacement is larger, so A's displacement is less than B's displacement.
